item.title: Bangladesh minister skips BIMSTEC's home ministers' meeting in Delhi
item.description:
Nearly three decades after its inception, home ministers of the seven-nation Bay of Bengal regional bloc, BIMSTEC, are set to hold their first-ever meeting in New Delhi next Tuesday.

However, Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed will not be attending.

A Bangladesh delegation led by the Senior Secretary of the Home Ministry, Monzur Morshed Chowdhury, will participate in his place.

BIMSTEC Secretary General Indra Mani Pandey confirmed the matter to Prothom Alo over the phone from Delhi on Sunday.

He stated that, excluding Bangladesh, the home ministers and state ministers of the other six member countries will participate in the meeting.

A day prior to the ministerial meeting, on 12 October, senior officials from the home ministries of the member states will sit for discussions for the first time.

Regarding the Bangladesh home minister's decision not to travel to Delhi, several senior government officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Prothom Alo that the decision was made in the context of the ongoing strain in bilateral relations with India.

Earlier in September, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman did not attend the outreach session of the BRICS summit held in Delhi. India had invited him to the session as the current chair of BIMSTEC.

However, the Bangladesh government clarified that the invitation was extended to him in his capacity as the BIMSTEC chair, not as the Prime Minister of Bangladesh.

BIMSTEC began its journey through the Bangkok Declaration on 6 June 1997, with the aim of acting as a bridge for cooperation between South and South-East Asia.

Its seven member states are Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, and Bhutan. The bloc's secretariat is located in Dhaka. Bangladesh assumed the chairmanship of BIMSTEC in April 2025.

Four nominated in official letter

The decision not to send Bangladesh's home minister is also reflected in an official diplomatic letter from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The letter, sent to the BIMSTEC Secretariat on 4 October, listed a four-member Bangladesh delegation for the meetings on 12 and 13 October. The home minister's name was not included on the list.

The letter sent to the BIMSTEC Secretariat stated that the delegation would be led by Home Ministry Senior Secretary Monzur Morshed Chowdhury.

Meanwhile, details about the meeting's preparations also surfaced from an urgent letter sent by the BIMSTEC Secretariat to the foreign ministries of the member countries on 5 October.

The letter noted that Bangladesh had submitted its delegation nominations on 4 October. As of 5 October, nominations had been received from Bangladesh, Bhutan and Sri Lanka. The remaining three countries—Myanmar, Nepal, and Thailand were urged to send their representatives' names promptly. Earlier, on 2 September, the BIMSTEC Secretariat had sent a letter requesting nominations from the member states.

Attendees at the Delhi meeting

According to the BIMSTEC Secretariat and diplomatic sources in Delhi, Indian Home Minister Amit Shah will chair the home minister-level meeting. The preceding day's meeting of senior home ministry officials will be conducted by India's Home Secretary, Govind Mohan.

Representing the other nations, Bhutan's Home Minister Lungten Dorji, Myanmar's Home Minister General Ko Ko Oo, Nepal's Home Minister Sudan Gurung, Sri Lanka's Home Minister Chandana Aberathne and Thailand's Deputy Minister of Interior Songsak Thongsri are scheduled to participate.

Terrorism and cross-border crime on the agenda

According to relevant sources, strengthening cooperation to combat terrorism and cross-border crime in the region will be a major focus at the Delhi meeting. Discussions will cover preventing human trafficking, drug smuggling, money laundering, and terror financing, as well as enhancing coordination among the law enforcement and security agencies of the member states.

The report and recommendations from the 11th meeting of the BIMSTEC Joint Working Group on Counter-Terrorism and Transnational Crime, held in Delhi on 28 and 29 September, will also feature prominently in the upcoming discussions.

A press release issued by the Indian Ministry of External Affairs on 29 September stated that representatives from all seven member countries, including Bangladesh, attended that meeting. It was chaired by Suhel Ajaz Khan, Additional Secretary (Counter Terrorism) at the Indian Ministry of External Affairs.

The meeting discussed traditional security threats in the region alongside emerging non-traditional ones. Several recommendations were made to boost cooperation in tackling terrorism and transnational crime.

Furthermore, the meeting reviewed reports from sub-groups dedicated to addressing human trafficking; preventing the illicit trade of narcotics and precursor chemicals; curbing money laundering and terror financing; fostering legal and law enforcement cooperation; and countering extremism and terrorism.

Decision made 8 years ago, first meeting now

The decision to hold a home minister-level meeting for BIMSTEC was made eight years ago. During the bloc's fourth summit in Kathmandu, Nepal, on 30 and 31 August 2018, leaders of the member states agreed to organise regular meetings at the home ministerial level.

The Kathmandu Declaration pledged to strengthen cooperation and coordination among the law enforcement agencies, intelligence bodies, and security institutions of the member countries. It was also decided to continue meetings at the National Security Advisor level alongside the home ministers' meetings.

However, no home minister-level meeting had taken place since that decision until now. A concept paper outlining the organisation of the home ministers' meeting was approved at the 20th BIMSTEC Ministerial Meeting in Bangkok in April 2025. Almost a year and a half later, the first such meeting is finally set to take place in Delhi.

item.title: Prof Samina Luthfa protests alleged harassment of teachers for expressing dissent
item.description:
Professor Samina Luthfa of the Department of Sociology at the University of Dhaka staged a five-minute silent protest in her classroom on Sunday, covering her mouth with a black cloth to protest attempts to curtail teachers’ freedom in the classroom and the alleged harassment of teachers for expressing dissent.

She staged the protest on Sunday, 11 October, and later described it in a post on her personal Facebook account.

In the post, Professor Samina Luthfa wrote that a planned conspiracy to undermine teachers’ freedom in the classroom was eroding trust in teacher-student relationships.

She said she had staged the protest in solidarity with teachers who had faced harassment for expressing dissent or speaking out.

Samina Luthfa also wrote that she had discussed and established a “code of conduct” with her students in the class. They discussed what could and could not be done in the classroom without permission and how disagreements should be resolved. She then sat silently for five minutes with a black cloth covering her mouth.

At the end of her post, Professor Samina Luthfa called on everyone to “reclaim the classroom”.

Earlier, on 7 October, a controversy arose over a discussion between Associate Professor Tasneem Siraj Mahboob of the Department of English at the University of Dhaka and a female student wearing a niqab during a class for final-semester postgraduate students.

Following a written complaint from students, an emergency meeting of the department on 8 October decided to bar the teacher from conducting classes. The courses she had been teaching were also redistributed among other teachers.

item.title: 8 flights from Dhaka cancelled; Biman to update on 2 on Monday
item.description:
Eight flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have so far been cancelled following an attack on King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital.

Apart from the cancellations, Biman Bangladesh Airlines will provide details about two of its flights at noon on Monday.

Biman Bangladesh Airlines announced the information in separate press releases issued on Sunday.

On Saturday night, Bangladesh time, the Iran-backed Houthi armed group in Yemen attacked King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia. It was the third attack on the airport this week. Following the incident, airport operations were suspended and all flights were diverted.

Shortly after the incident, Biman Bangladesh Airlines announced the suspension of flights BG339 and BG340.

In a statement issued on Sunday, the national flag carrier said the airport authorities had extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport until 9:00 pm UTC on 11 October. In Bangladesh time, the suspension will remain in effect until 3:00 am on Monday.

As of Sunday afternoon, the eight cancelled flights included two operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, one by US-Bangla Airlines, three by Saudia and two by Riyadh Air.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), a total of 2,951 passengers were booked on these flights.

Reporting the suspension of flights at Riyadh’s international airport, Reuters said the airport authorities had advised passengers to contact their respective airlines before travelling to the airport and to check the latest status of their flights.

item.title: New attack hits Riyadh airport, says Saudi coalition
item.description:
Riyadh airport came under fresh attack on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said, a day after a strike blamed on the Iran-backed group killed 12 people.
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 at King Khalid International Airport, causing a fire, and that the relevant authorities were responding at the scene.
He added in a post on X that air defences had "intercepted and destroyed" a cruise missile near the airport.
Earlier, AFP journalists heard a powerful explosion in central Riyadh, while three residents in the city's north later reported hearing another blast.
"The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook," a resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in northern Riyadh told AFP.
Residents also said they saw ambulances heading towards the airport, which lies in the northeast of the capital.
A Riyadh Metro official told AFP that the capital's authorities had suspended transit service to two of the three stations serving the airport. The official said the decision would be "reviewed on a daily basis".
Saturday's attack on Riyadh airport was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Saudi Arabia backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis, who captured swathes of Red Sea coastline in a lightning offensive last month.

item.title: Saudi Arabia on war footing after deadly airport strike
item.description:
Two Bangladeshis were among 12 people killed in a missile attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while four other Bangladeshis are fighting for recovery in intensive care as the deadliest strike on the kingdom in more than a decade threatens to draw the United States deeper into the escalating Middle East conflict.
The attack on Saturday left at least 309 people injured, forced the closure of one of the region’s busiest aviation hubs and triggered widespread international condemnation.
The two Bangladeshis killed were identified as Md Shahed Ahmed of Madla village in Bogura’s Shahjahanpur upazila and Md Nasrullah Badarpuri of Badarpur village in Cumilla’s Nangalkot upazila, according to Bangladesh’s foreign ministry.
Four other Bangladeshis were receiving treatment in the intensive care unit of King Khalid Hospital in Riyadh, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam confirmed on Sunday.
The attack, the third on Riyadh’s international airport within a week, prompted Saudi Arabia to threaten a decisive military response, while Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi movement renewed warnings that Saudi airports and airspace remained vulnerable to further strikes.
US President Donald Trump said Washington was considering joining Saudi military operations against the Houthis, raising fears that the renewed fighting in Yemen could further widen the regional war.
The disruption has also reached Bangladesh, with at least five flights from Dhaka cancelled and Biman Bangladesh Airlines suspending its Riyadh services.
Bangladesh’s foreign ministry said a missile struck Terminal 3 of King Khalid International Airport at approximately 3:20pm local time on Saturday, when passengers from several countries, including Bangladesh, were waiting inside.
Shahed Ahmed was from Madla village in Shahjahanpur, Bogura, while Nasrullah Badarpuri was from Badarpur village in Nangalkot, Cumilla.
The government is working with Saudi authorities to assist the victims and contact their families.
Speaking to journalists in Dhaka on Sunday, State Minister Shama Obaed said Bangladesh’s diplomatic missions in Riyadh and Jeddah were coordinating with Saudi officials to identify the injured and ensure necessary treatment.
She said 14 Bangladeshis had died in the wider Middle East conflict so far, highlighting the growing risks faced by expatriate workers.
“We have already lost 14 Bangladeshis in this war. We do not want any more of our remittance warriors to die,” she said.
The government will bear the costs of repatriating the bodies of the deceased Bangladeshis, she added.
At least 82 uninjured Bangladeshi passengers were being accommodated at hotels and other facilities, including the Marriott and Radisson hotels and Princess Nourah University.
Bangladesh strongly condemned the attack, describing assaults on civilians and civilian infrastructure as unacceptable.
The foreign ministry called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and a diplomatic resolution to the escalating crisis.
The missile struck an airport complex housing Terminals 3 and 4, according to an official cited by the Associated Press.
The dead included four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one citizen each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Palestine, Syria and Sudan.
Witnesses described scenes of panic as an explosion struck the terminal, sending passengers running for safety.
One passenger told AFP that a nearby departure gate had been hit and that injured people were lying on the ground.
Another injured traveller told Reuters that part of the ceiling near a departure gate collapsed after an object crossed the sky outside.
Ambulances and helicopters transported casualties to hospitals across Riyadh, where emergency departments faced a sudden influx of patients.
Saudi health authorities activated emergency medical arrangements to treat the wounded, some of whom remained in critical condition.
Saturday’s strike followed two earlier attacks on the same airport during the week, which had already caused fatalities and seriously damaged a Saudi commercial aircraft parked on the tarmac.
The repeated strikes have raised questions about the vulnerability of civilian aviation infrastructure to missiles and drones despite Saudi Arabia’s extensive air-defence capabilities.
King Khalid International Airport remained closed on Sunday as authorities assessed damage and security risks.
The closure forced airlines to cancel or divert hundreds of flights, stranding passengers and disrupting international connections.
Bangladesh’s Civil Aviation Authority confirmed that three additional flights from Dhaka had been cancelled on Sunday, following two cancellations on Saturday.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines suspended its Dhaka-Riyadh-Dhaka services until further notice.
The disruption also affected flights operated by other carriers serving the Bangladesh-Saudi Arabia route.
Saudi authorities extended the airport closure into early Monday, although the exact timing of the resumption of operations remained uncertain.
International airlines, including Emirates, Etihad Airways and Lufthansa Group carriers, announced cancellations or extended suspensions of Riyadh services.
The crisis has particular implications for Bangladesh, given the large number of migrant workers and religious travellers using Saudi aviation routes.
Saudi authorities also moved schools in Riyadh to remote learning for the week as security concerns persisted.
Foreign embassies, including those of the United States, United Kingdom and Canada, advised their citizens to avoid the airport.
The Saudi-led military coalition blamed the Houthis for Saturday’s strike and promised a firm response.
Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki described the attack as a war crime, saying civilian passengers and airport workers had been targeted.
The Houthis had not explicitly claimed responsibility for Saturday’s deadly strike in the initial reports, although they acknowledged earlier attacks on Saudi airports and continued threatening aviation facilities.
On Sunday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree renewed warnings to airlines, airport employees and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, with the exception of facilities serving Mecca and Medina.
The Houthi-run foreign ministry warned that further Saudi military action in Yemen would provoke stronger retaliation.
The Saudi-led coalition also reported a projectile falling near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and said it intercepted a drone in the eastern region on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Houthi-controlled media reported another suspected Saudi strike on Sanaa airport in Yemen.
The report could not immediately be independently verified, and Saudi authorities had not commented on the allegation.
The attack has increased pressure on Washington to provide greater military support to Saudi Arabia.
Asked whether the United States might join Saudi strikes against the Houthis, Trump said on Saturday that the option remained under consideration.
“We may. We’re going to look at it,” he told reporters, adding that a decision could be made quickly.
Trump also indicated that he planned to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned the airport attacks and expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres also condemned the killing of civilians, warning that attacks on civilian infrastructure violate international law.
The European Union, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Pakistan and several other countries issued statements condemning the strike.
UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg warned that attacks on civilian airports represented a serious escalation that threatened regional security and complicated efforts to restore peace.
The latest violence follows the collapse of a ceasefire that had largely contained fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis since 2022.
Saudi Arabia entered Yemen’s civil war in 2015, leading a military coalition supporting the internationally recognised Yemeni government against the Houthis, who control the capital, Sanaa.
The conflict caused widespread destruction and a humanitarian catastrophe before the ceasefire brought relative calm.
Fighting resumed this summer as the Houthis launched attacks on Saudi targets and captured strategic territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial maritime passage connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces launched a counteroffensive last week to regain territory, supported by Saudi airstrikes.
The Houthis have retaliated with attacks on Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and other facilities.
The confrontation is unfolding alongside the broader war involving Iran, the United States and Israel, which began in February.
With Iran-aligned Houthi forces threatening shipping through Bab el-Mandeb and tensions already affecting the Strait of Hormuz, further escalation could disrupt global energy supplies and international trade.
Saudi Arabia is also facing mounting pressure over its air defences as repeated strikes expose civilian facilities to attack.
Despite the security crisis, Riyadh proceeded with preparations for the WPC Energy Congress, bringing together ministers and energy executives from around the world.
The immediate concern, however, remains the safety of civilians and travellers as both sides threaten further military action.
For Bangladesh, the deaths of two nationals, the critical condition of four others and the disruption of flights have brought the consequences of the widening Middle East conflict directly home.

item.title: Home minister to skip Bimstec meeting in Delhi
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed will not attend the first-ever meeting of home ministers from the seven-member Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (Bimstec) in New Delhi on Tuesday.
Instead, a Bangladesh delegation led by Home Affairs Senior Secretary Manzur Morshed Chowdhury will attend the meeting, reports Bangla Tribune.
The two-day meeting will begin on Monday with senior officials from the home ministries of Bimstec member states. Home ministers and state ministers from the member countries will meet the following day, nearly three decades after the regional bloc was established.
The Bangladesh delegation will also include AKM Shahidul Karim, additional secretary for Saarc, Bimstec and other priority issues at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Rebecca Khan, joint secretary at the Ministry of Home Affairs.
In September, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also skipped the outreach session of the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had invited him to the session in his capacity as Bimstec chair.
Bangladesh assumed the Bimstec chairmanship in April 2025.
The inaugural meeting of home ministers of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) will review regional security cooperation and explore ways to expand it under the regional grouping, officials said.
The meeting will bring together ministers and representatives from the seven BIMSTEC member states - Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
Bhutan’s home minister, Myanmar’s union minister for Home Affairs, Nepal’s home minister, Sri Lanka’s minister for Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs, and Thailand’s deputy secretary-general of the National Security Council are expected to attend, an official told UNB.
The meeting comes as BIMSTEC seeks to strengthen regional cooperation in law enforcement, intelligence sharing and security.
At the fourth BIMSTEC Summit, held in Kathmandu on August 30-31, 2018, the leaders expressed their determination to strengthen cooperation and coordination among law enforcement, intelligence and security agencies.
They also decided to hold meetings of BIMSTEC Home Ministers while continuing meetings of BIMSTEC National Security Chiefs to promote cooperation and coordination in combating terrorism and transnational crime.
The BIMSTEC home ministers’ meeting will be supported by a senior officials’ Meeting of home and interior ministries.

item.title: BNP seeks unity in local government elections
item.description:
The BNP wants to contest the upcoming local government elections united, avoiding internal rivalries and divisions within the party. To this end, the party is emphasizing the selection of a single candidate in each area, giving priority to grassroots opinions and resolving potential disputes in advance.
The party's highest policymaking body, the National Standing Committee, also discussed the need to complete administrative and organizational preparations before the elections.
The issues were discussed at a committee meeting held at the BNP chairman's political office in Gulshan, Dhaka, on Saturday night. Chaired by BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, the meeting also discussed security arrangements for the upcoming Durga Puja and various organizational matters.
Party sources said leaders exchanged views on competition among potential candidates at the grassroots level, the risk of votes being split among party members and election preparations.
The possibility of internal disputes arising from multiple candidates contesting the same position received particular attention. Since local government elections will not be held under party symbols, more than 1 BNP leader may contest for the same post, potentially splitting votes and prolonging local rivalries after the elections.
To avoid such a situation, the party has emphasized resolving differences through discussions in advance and selecting a single candidate for each position.
According to party sources, the BNP wants to ensure a fair and impartial electoral environment so voters can cast their ballots for candidates of their choice. At the same time, the party is prioritizing unity among its leaders and activists to ensure they work together during the election campaign.
The BNP plans to prioritize 4 criteria when selecting candidates for the local government elections: a clean public image, popularity, contributions and sacrifices for the party, and the likelihood of winning.
Sources said leaders had been instructed to gather information about potential candidates at the local level and prepare lists based on field-level surveys as part of the initial selection process. The party is also emphasizing the need to assess candidates' acceptability by collecting opinions from local residents and party leaders and activists.
To oversee the process, the BNP has formed a 4-member committee comprising Standing Committee member Nazrul Islam Khan, Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, Standing Committee member Ismail Zabiullah and Special Secretary Belayet Hossain Mridha.
The committee members have already held online meetings with leaders from the Chittagong, Barisal, Khulna, Rangpur and Mymensingh divisions. Discussions focused on the party's position at the local level, potential candidates and election preparations.
The committee plans to hold similar meetings with leaders from the remaining divisions.
According to party sources, if inconsistencies are found in the lists of potential candidates, the lists will be sent to divisional-level teams for review. If the issues remain unresolved, they will be discussed with the central leadership before a decision is made.
The aim is to select acceptable candidates while avoiding disputes over nominations.
The timing of the local government elections and the preparations required to hold them were also discussed at the Standing Committee meeting.
Party sources said several leaders argued that administrative and organizational preparations were necessary to restore local government institutions to effective functioning after prolonged disruptions at various levels.
Some committee members, however, called for the necessary preparations to be completed as soon as possible so the elections could be held without unnecessary delay.
The possibility of the Election Commission announcing a tentative schedule was also discussed, according to party sources.
Some members said the government needed to assign the Election Commission the necessary responsibility for organizing the local government elections. They also raised questions about the authority to announce election dates if the government had not formally assigned that responsibility.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi and Standing Committee member Ismail Zabiullah recently briefed the party chairman on discussions held online with leaders from district, metropolitan, upazila and municipal units.
The discussions covered grassroots preparations, potential candidates and organizational coordination.
The government has previously said it was preparing to hold local government elections early next year.
On September 24, Election Commissioner Md Anwarul Islam Sarker said the commission was considering holding the elections in January, after students' annual examinations. The plan is to begin the local government election process with Union Parishad polls.
Bangladesh has 5 types of local government institutions where elections are held: Union Parishads, municipalities, upazila parishads, district councils and city corporations.
Asked about the preparations, BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said grassroots preparations for local government elections were complete, with candidates to be selected based on public engagement, local acceptability and support among party leaders and activists.

item.title: Minister orders action against passenger harassment during Puja holidays
item.description:
Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam has directed authorities to coordinate preparations across road, rail and waterways to ensure safe and hassle-free travel during the five-day Durga Puja holiday.
He also ordered strict measures against excessive fares, passenger harassment and ticket black marketing.
The minister issued the directives while chairing a meeting at the Road Transport and Highways Division in Dhaka on Sunday afternoon to ensure safe and smooth travel during the festival.
He said all necessary measures must be taken to ensure the peaceful celebration of Sharadiya Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community.
With passenger traffic expected to rise during the five-day holiday, the minister urged authorities to remain vigilant and make the best use of existing resources and experience to ensure safe, comfortable and uninterrupted journeys.
He stressed that excessive fares, passenger harassment and other untoward incidents must not spoil the festive atmosphere, calling on all concerned to perform their duties responsibly.
The meeting reviewed preparations to manage the expected surge in passenger traffic, including measures to curb excessive fares, launch special bus services by the Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC), keep sufficient ferries ready and conduct mobile court drives to prevent irregularities.
Authorities were also directed to deploy adequate law enforcement personnel at bridge toll plazas.
The minister instructed officials to carry out temporary repairs on key roads around Dhaka to keep them traffic-worthy. He also ordered the introduction of three pairs of special trains on the Dhaka–Chittagong and Cox’s Bazar routes, based on passenger demand, and additional coaches on other routes.
Measures to prevent ticket black marketing were also discussed.
The meeting emphasised preparations to manage crowds and traffic during idol immersion ceremonies and ensure security across road, rail and waterways.
State Minister for Railways and the Road Transport and Highways Division Habibul Rashid, and State Minister for Shipping and the Bridges Division Md Rajib Ahsan, attended the meeting as special guests.
Railways Secretary Md Fahimul Islam, Road Transport and Highways Division Secretary Dr Mohammad Ziaul Haque, Shipping Ministry Secretary Zakaria, and representatives of relevant government agencies, bus owners’ associations and the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust were also present.
The minister urged all relevant agencies to work in close coordination and discharge their responsibilities effectively, expressing hope that Durga Puja would be celebrated peacefully and holidaymakers would enjoy safe and comfortable journeys.

item.title: Delhi protests defy crackdown as Supreme Court intervenes
item.description:
Protests demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar continued across New Delhi for a second consecutive day on Saturday, with hundreds detained despite Supreme Court intervention against unlawful arrests, as opposition leader Rahul Gandhi announced another major mobilization on Sunday.
The fresh demonstrations followed on Saturday’s sweeping police crackdown, when nearly 7,000 people, including four former chief ministers, were detained while attempting to join a protest organised by the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
According to Reuters, police detained hundreds of protesters on Saturday as students and activists staged demonstrations at several locations across the capital, defying heavy security and restrictions around Jantar Mantar.
India on Sunday reported that around 200 people were detained on Saturday, including members of the Students’ Federation of India, All India Students’ Association and Krantikari Yuva Sangathan.
Among those detained were Communist Party of India (Marxist) lawmaker John Brittas and student leader Neha Bora.
The Indian Express reported that police intercepted groups of demonstrators chanting slogans against the Election Commission and forced several into waiting buses.
Some protesters alleged they were manhandled, while others claimed they had been detained despite not participating in demonstrations. Reuters said it could not independently verify allegations of police assaults.
In a significant development, India’s Supreme Court held a special sitting on Saturday and directed authorities to prevent unlawful detentions of peaceful protesters.
The court also instructed the government to ensure that Delhi Metro services operated normally and internet facilities remained uninterrupted, subject to lawful public-order restrictions.
According to India on Sunday, the court issued notice to the central government on a petition alleging violations of earlier judicial directions concerning transport restrictions.
All Metro stations remained open on Saturday, although roads approaching sensitive areas continued to be barricaded.
Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and senior leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released on Saturday after being produced before an executive magistrate.
Reuters reported that the three were released on an undertaking to maintain public peace.
Delhi Police said a Rs50,000 surety bond had been furnished, requiring them to maintain peace and good behaviour for one year.
The leaders had been detained on Saturday after their aircraft landed in Delhi.
Following their release, CJP representatives announced that demonstrations would continue and expand nationwide.
At a press conference, Das accused authorities of suppressing peaceful dissent, while Ranka reiterated the movement’s demand for Kumar’s resignation.
Delhi Police, meanwhile, said 20 cases had been registered over on Saturday’s demonstrations, including allegations of assaulting officers and obstructing public servants.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi announced on Saturday that leaders of the opposition INDIA bloc would march to the Supreme Court on Sunday to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant.
According to India Today, the opposition will demand an end to alleged electoral manipulation, suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls and Kumar’s resignation.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said opposition leaders had sought a meeting with the chief justice.
Saturday’s crackdown saw former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee, Arvind Kejriwal, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar detained, according to The Indian Express.
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, lawyer Prashant Bhushan and activist Yogendra Yadav were also among those detained.
The controversy centres on the Election Commission’s revision of electoral rolls, which opposition parties allege has excluded large numbers of legitimate voters and disproportionately benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Election Commission has maintained that the revision is intended to improve the accuracy of voter lists.
With fresh demonstrations planned and judicial scrutiny intensifying, the confrontation over India’s electoral system appears set to continue into the new week.

item.title: Bus owners step in to tackle Dhaka’s traffic chaos
item.description:
Bus owners and workers have taken to the streets at 20 points across Dhaka in a bid to bring order to the capital’s chaotic traffic, enforcing designated bus stops and preventing passengers from getting on and off buses at random spots.
The drive, launched on Sunday by the Dhaka Road Transport Owners Association, also aims to improve road discipline and prevent the operation of unfit, dilapidated and permitless buses.
Teams comprising bus owners and workers have been deployed in areas including Mirpur, ECB Chattar, Karwan Bazar, Farmgate, Shahbagh, Paltan, Motijheel, Gulistan and Jatrabari. Association leaders have also been visiting different locations to monitor the activities.
At Shahbagh intersection, several people wearing orange vests bearing the association's name were seen directing bus drivers with sticks.
A bus owner involved in the drive said they had repeatedly instructed drivers and helpers not to stop buses outside designated points to pick up or drop off passengers, but the instructions had not been followed.
“Drivers and helpers do not listen to us. We have repeatedly told them not to stop buses wherever they please to pick up passengers. That is why we, the owners, have taken to the streets to bring the situation under control,” he said.
According to the association, a separate drive was conducted in Gulistan on Sunday morning against buses with broken windows, damaged paintwork and expired fitness certificates.
Jahangir Sikder, convener of the Gulistan Bus Terminal Transport Owners Association and vice-president of the Dhaka Road Transport Owners Association, and Alamgir Kabir, member-secretary of the Gulistan Bus Terminal Owners Association, led the drive.
Meanwhile, SM Sohrab Hossain, convener of the Mirpur Regional Owners Association, inspected activities at Kalsi intersection as part of efforts to ease congestion and improve road discipline.
ASM Ahmed Khokon, general secretary of the Bangladesh Road Transport Owners Association and treasurer of the Dhaka Road Transport Owners Association, told Dhaka Tribune that the initiative was launched in response to long-standing complaints about buses stopping outside designated points.
“We have repeatedly instructed our drivers not to stop anywhere other than designated stops. We are also raising awareness among passengers, asking them to wait at designated stops and not get on or off buses wherever they please,” he said.
Khokon said the association would continue the drive until discipline was restored on the roads.
“We have started this initiative at around 20 points across Dhaka. We will continue until we can bring discipline to the roads. I have been at Shahbagh intersection since 8am, and bus owners and workers are all involved in this effort,” he added.
The initiative follows a meeting held last Thursday, chaired by the prime minister, to discuss the implementation of the bus route rationalisation plan.
The Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority (DTCA), Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) and bus owners' associations were assigned responsibility for implementing the plan.
Road Transport and Bridges Minister Shaikh Robiul Alam said he had met bus company owners and association leaders on September 28 to discuss company-based bus operations and compliance with vehicle fitness requirements and traffic laws.
According to bus owners, the meeting produced seven decisions.
Buses in Dhaka will operate through companies, with the government dealing directly with them rather than individual owners to ensure accountability.
Companies will be held responsible for unfit buses, traffic violations and other irregularities. Owners who break the rules may be expelled from their companies, and their buses will face legal action.
The owners' association will work to stop excessive bookings at bus counters, trip-based extortion and other unethical financial collection.
Companies that fail to improve services and drivers' conduct within the stipulated period may lose their route permits, with the government introducing new companies or alternative arrangements.
Bus owners must repair and repaint all buses operating in Dhaka within two months. The association will oversee the work, and buses not repaired by the deadline will be taken off the road.
The association will also form area-based teams with the DMP to prevent the operation of illegal, dilapidated and permitless buses and those violating route regulations.
Other measures include ensuring buses operate through designated counters and stop at designated points for passenger pick-ups and drop-offs.
Bus owners' and workers' organisations have also been asked to discuss company-based operations with relevant stakeholders within 15 days.
Despite several initiatives to address traffic congestion in Dhaka, the problem continues to cause significant economic losses. An earlier World Bank estimate put the number of working hours lost to traffic congestion in the capital at around 3.2 million a day.
Urban planners now estimate that the figure has exceeded 5 million hours a day, with annual economic losses surpassing Tk37,000 crore.
The association said its latest initiative would continue until discipline was restored to the city's roads.

item.title: Sajek Valley closed indefinitely over security concerns
item.description:
The Rangamati district administration has temporarily closed Sajek Valley, a popular tourist destination, from 6pm on Sunday until further notice, citing security concerns.
The decision was announced in an emergency notice signed by Rangamati Deputy Commissioner Najma Ashrafi on Sunday evening.
The notice asked tourists currently staying in Sajek, under Baghaichhari upazila of Rangamati, to leave the area by 5pm on Tuesday, and return safely to their respective destinations.
The closure will remain in effect until further notice due to unforeseen and unavoidable circumstances, the notice said.
The deputy commissioner said the decision was taken with tourists' overall safety in mind. Sajek Valley will reopen once the situation returns to normal, she added.
According to the district administration and local sources, a convoy of tourist vehicles was stranded on the road for around three hours on Sunday amid protests by two local organisations in Sajek.
The vehicles were able to reach their destinations after protesters withdrew following discussions with police and army personnel.
At around 2:30pm on Sunday, a convoy leaving Sajek became stranded at Ujobaazar, while vehicles heading towards Sajek from Khagrachhari town were held up at Machalong Bazar.
Protesters blocked roads at both locations. They withdrew at around 5:30pm, allowing traffic to resume.
On Saturday, the Sajek Karbari Association and the Sajek Public Rights Protection Committee announced a blockade in the area, which began at 6am on Sunday.
The protesters blocked the main road connecting Sajek Valley to other areas. They placed tree trunks across the road and set tyres on fire at several points in support of the program, disrupting traffic.
The two organisations alleged that the regional political group JSS (Santu Larma) had begun armed activities in the area and was threatening and intimidating local residents.
They said they had held a rally last Thursday and set a deadline for action against the alleged activities. As no action was taken, they called the road blockade, according to the organisations.

item.title: Customs recovers 1,054 grams of jewelry and 720 precious stones at airport
item.description:
Dhaka Customs House recovered 1,054 grams of jewelry and 720 precious stones hidden in a jar of pickles at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on Saturday night.
The passenger, Md Johnny Rahman, was detained and later shown arrested in a case filed over the incident.
Kamrul Islam, deputy commissioner of Dhaka Customs House, confirmed the information to Dhaka Tribune on Sunday. He said the passenger arrived in Dhaka from Kolkata on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight and that officials recovered the items during a search of his luggage.
According to a press release issued by Dhaka Customs House on Sunday, the passenger was detained at around 8:30pm on Saturday.
The customs house said its preventive team had stepped up surveillance at various points in the airport following a tip-off. The passenger's bag was scanned as he crossed the green channel after immigration without declaring any baggage.
The scan detected metallic objects inside a jar of pickles in his luggage. Customs officials then opened and searched the baggage, recovering the jewelry and precious stones.
The recovered items included 389 gold rings set with 18-carat diamonds, 151 platinum rings of 950 purity, 3 pieces of white gold jewelry, 2 silver rings, 5 gold lockets, 1 chain and 472 nose pins.
Officials also recovered 720 precious stones, including diamonds, rubies and topaz of various sizes, weighing 45 carats in total. They also found 23 certification cards used to verify the authenticity of the jewelry.
Dhaka Customs House has filed a criminal case against the passenger with Airport Police Station over the incident.

item.title: Pawan Badhe: Strong Dhaka-Delhi relations can contribute to regional peace
item.description:
Acting Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Pawan Badhe on Sunday said strong Bangladesh-India relations can contribute to regional peace, prosperity and people-to-people understanding.
“India and Bangladesh share a language of the heart: a history, a culture, a river system, and a future. Our relationship is wide, covering trade, connectivity, energy, education, health, and the bond between our people,” he said.
The acting Indian envoy made the remarks at a function marking the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi and the International Day of Non-Violence at the Liberation War Museum.
Water Resources Minister Md Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee attended the discussion as the chief guest. Barrister AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon, MP, and Gandhi Ashram Trustee Board Chairman Major General Jiban Kanai Das (retd), among others, also spoke.
Pawan Badhe said Gandhi’s relevance in the contemporary world is profound. “At a time marked by geopolitical tensions, armed conflicts, environmental challenges and social inequalities, Gandhi’s principles offer a moral compass for humanity,” he said.
He said Gandhi’s belief in simple living, ethical leadership, truth and service to the most vulnerable challenged people to measure progress not merely by economic growth but also by compassion, justice and human welfare. “His life reminds us that moral courage can be more powerful than physical force,” he said.
Pawan Badhe shared three ideas of Gandhi that he said were extremely relevant to the present time.
“Gandhi never saw non-violence as weakness. He called it the weapon of the strong, because it takes more courage to hold your ground without hatred than to strike. In an age of polarisation, his lesson is that we can disagree firmly and still remain humane,” he said.
The acting envoy said the United Nations' recognition of Gandhi’s birth anniversary as the International Day of Non-Violence demonstrated how widely this principle is valued.
He highlighted the primacy of truth, noting that Gandhi titled his autobiography “The Story of My Experiments with Truth.”
“He believed that public life without honesty is hollow. Today, when a falsehood can circle the globe before the truth has dressed, his insistence on integrity, in speech, in politics, and in what we share online, is not old-fashioned. It is essential,” Pawan Badhe said.
“He reminded us that the earth provides enough for everyone's need, but not for everyone's greed. South Asia is among the regions most exposed to climate change, from rising seas along our coasts to floods and cyclones that respect no border,” he said.
Pawan Badhe said Gandhi’s ideas about simple living, local self-reliance and the responsible use of shared resources directly addressed the challenges facing both Bangladesh and India.
He also highlighted Gandhi’s close ties with Bengal’s intellectual world, particularly his relationship with Rabindranath Tagore, who is equally cherished in Bangladesh and India.
He said their relationship was marked by mutual respect and friendly disagreement.
“Tagore gave him the name ‘Mahatma’. Their conversations show that two great minds can differ and still enrich each other. That is a good model for our two countries, and for the region,” the Indian diplomat said.
He noted that Gandhi’s spirit of dialogue, mutual respect and shared well-being offered guidance for strengthening bilateral relations and building a better future for the region.

item.title: Preparations near completion at Lalon shrine ahead of 136th death anniversary
item.description:
Preparations are nearing completion at Lalon Shrine in Cheuriya of Kumarkhali upazila in Kushtia ahead of the 136th death anniversary (Tirodhan Dibash) of Baul emperor Fakir Lalon Shah.
A three-day memorial festival will begin at Lalon Akhrabari on October 17.
Painting, decoration, stage construction and cleaning activities are progressing at the shrine, while traders have started arriving to set up stalls for the occasion.
Abdur Razzaq Bachchu, a member of the Lalon Academy's death anniversary organizing committee, told BSS that all preparations would be completed on time.
Lalon devotee Sabur said the occasion was more than a festival, describing it as an opportunity for spiritual purification and a celebration of humanity.
Devotees and spiritual practitioners from different parts of the country have already begun arriving at the shrine, creating a festive atmosphere.
Kushtia Deputy Commissioner Touhid Bin Hasan said Lalon's death anniversary reflects the country's folk culture, humanism and secular spirit.
He said devotees, spiritual practitioners and visitors from home and abroad gather at the shrine every year to observe the occasion.
The district administration has taken necessary measures to ensure security and facilitate the peaceful and smooth celebration of the festival, he added.

item.title: Police recover German tourist’s stolen laptop, bag in Natore
item.description:
Police have recovered a laptop and a bag containing valuables stolen from German national Kirill Lander Weber at Natore Railway Station.
Superintendent of Police Mohammad Shariful Haque confirmed the matter on Sunday.
The items were recovered from Noor Garments, a shop in the Nicha Bazar area of Natore town, around 8pm on Sunday, reports Bangla Tribune.
On Wednesday, Kirill travelled by train to Natore via Santahar after visiting several heritage sites in Bogura. At Natore Railway Station, a young man wearing a yellow vest approached him, claiming to be a railway employee, and gained his trust through conversation.
Kirill left his bag with the man in the station’s waiting room before going to an ATM booth to withdraw money and buy a ticket for a train to Darshana. When he returned, both the man and his bag were missing.
The bag contained a laptop, a DSLR camera and other valuables. Kirill had planned to enter India through the Gede border crossing after reaching Darshana.
Following the incident, police collected CCTV footage from the station and identified the suspect. Teams from Natore district police, railway police, Special Response Battalion (SRB-5) and Rajshahi Metropolitan Police subsequently launched efforts to arrest him and recover the belongings.
Earlier, officials said the investigation was complicated by the absence of a trackable mobile phone in the stolen bag, making it difficult to locate the suspect.
SRB-5 had also announced a reward for information leading to the suspect’s identification and arrest. On Saturday night, the unit put up posters featuring the suspect’s image at key locations around Natore Railway Station after analysing CCTV footage.
Hafiz Al Asad, commander of SRB-5’s Natore camp, confirmed the reward announcement and said efforts to arrest the suspect were continuing.

item.title: Sobhana’s historic ton in vain as Australia seal ODI series
item.description:
Sobhana Mostary struck a record-breaking century but Bangladesh Women suffered a nine-wicket defeat against Australia in the second ODI in Brisbane on Sunday, as the hosts chased down 221 with 131 balls to spare to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.
Sobhana scored 118 off 134 balls, hitting 18 fours, to register the highest individual score by a Bangladesh batter in women’s ODIs. Her remarkable innings rescued the visitors from a disastrous start and helped them post 220 for six after losing three wickets for just eight runs.
However, Georgia Voll’s unbeaten 131 off 97 balls and Phoebe Litchfield’s 70 off 51 deliveries powered Australia to 222 for one in just 28.1 overs, extending their winning streak at Allan Border Field to 23 matches.
Bangladesh’s innings appeared to be heading for an early collapse as Megan Schutt and Kim Garth dismantled the top order. Fargana Hoque fell for a 13-ball duck, Sarmin Sultana scored five and Sharmin Akhter departed without scoring, leaving the visitors in deep trouble inside eight overs.
Sobhana, however, responded with remarkable composure and attacking intent. Joining captain Nigar Sultana Joty, she gradually took control of the innings, finding boundaries against both pace and spin while Joty provided support at the other end.
The pair added 195 runs for the fourth wicket, the highest women’s ODI partnership at the Brisbane ground, transforming Bangladesh’s position and frustrating the Australian bowlers.
Sobhana reached her maiden ODI century off 123 balls before eventually falling to Schutt in the 48th over. Her 118 surpassed Bangladesh’s previous highest individual score in women’s ODIs and marked a significant milestone for the team against the world’s top-ranked side.
Joty remained unbeaten on 74 off 114 balls, striking seven fours, as Bangladesh finished on 220 for six. Schutt was Australia’s most successful bowler, claiming four wickets for 36 runs.
The visitors, however, had little answer to Australia’s aggressive chase. Voll and Litchfield added 162 runs for the opening wicket in just 19.5 overs, taking the game away from Bangladesh before Litchfield fell for 70.
Voll continued unabated, reaching her third ODI century before guiding Australia home alongside Ellyse Perry, who finished unbeaten on 19.
Despite the defeat, Sobhana’s historic innings offered Bangladesh a significant individual milestone, even as the team’s struggle to contain Australia’s batting underlined the gap they must bridge to compete consistently against the world’s leading sides.
Brief Score
Australia 222 for 1 (Voll 131*, Litchfield 70, Akter 1-32) beat Bangladesh 220 for 6 (Mostary 118, Nigar 74*, Schutt 4-36) by nine wickets

item.title: Hasan’s hat-trick puts Bangladesh in command
item.description:
Hasan Mahmud scripted history with a maiden hat-trick by a Bangladesh pacer in Test cricket and became the fastest Bangladeshi to 50 wickets in the format as the visitors strengthened their grip on the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi on Sunday.
Bangladesh reached 223-6 in their second innings at stumps on the third day at Sheikh Zayed Stadium, extending their overall lead to 329 runs after bowling Afghanistan out for 240.
Hasan, who claimed five wickets for 55 runs, delivered a decisive burst in the morning session, removing Ismat Alam, Qais Ahmad and Zia-ur-Rehman in three consecutive deliveries in the 83rd over to become only the third Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test hat-trick.
Leg-spinner Alok Kapali had claimed Bangladesh’s first Test hat-trick against Pakistan in Peshawar in 2003, while off-spinner Sohag Gazi achieved the feat against New Zealand in Dhaka in 2013.
Hasan’s achievement was particularly significant as Bangladesh’s pace attack continued to establish itself as a formidable force in Test cricket. He also reached the 50-wicket milestone in the format, underlining his growing importance to the national side.
“When you start bowling, you try to bowl upright, swing the ball and get wickets. I was just trying that and bowling across,” Hasan said after the day’s play.
“I’m very pleased to see this kind of moment in the morning. Yesterday, I got one wicket in the whole day, but I wasn’t nervous at all. I was looking forward. I just felt that I should bowl straight, that’s it, and let the ball do its job.”
Afghanistan had appeared well placed to build a substantial first-innings total, with captain Rahmat Shah anchoring the innings. Rahmat remained unbeaten on 105 off 216 balls, but received little support from the lower order as the hosts lost their last six wickets for just 29 runs.
Hasan’s hat-trick reduced Afghanistan to 220-8, and Ebadot Hossain completed the demolition by taking four wickets for 56 runs. Mehidy Hasan Miraz claimed the other wicket as Afghanistan were dismissed in 89.1 overs.
Bangladesh had earlier posted 346 in their first innings, with Tanzid Hasan Tamim scoring 83, Shadman Islam making 67 and Litton Das contributing 53.
The visitors initially struggled in their second innings, slipping to 53-3 after Shadman, Mominul Haque and Tanzid departed cheaply. However, Mushfiqur Rahim and captain Najmul Hossain Shanto steadied the innings with a 159-run fourth-wicket partnership.
Mushfiqur, who had been dismissed for a duck in the first innings, scored 81 off 148 balls, hitting nine fours. Shanto made a patient 82 from 191 deliveries before falling late in the day.
Bangladesh lost three wickets in the final 10 overs, including Mushfiqur and Shanto, but Litton remained unbeaten on five alongside Mehidy, who was yet to score.
Reflecting on the historic morning, Hasan credited his teammates for helping him make the right decisions during the hat-trick over.
“Credit to the captain and Litton Das for talking and chatting with each other. They corrected me, saying it was going to hit, so I could take the review,” he said.
Hasan also looked ahead to Bangladesh’s upcoming Test assignments, including the World Test Championship and the tour of South Africa.
“I just want to keep going like that always,” he said, adding that the team would continue to focus on bowling the right lengths and maintaining the same process.
With a 329-run advantage and four wickets remaining, Bangladesh are firmly positioned to dictate the final two days, while Afghanistan face a formidable challenge to save the Test.

item.title: UN, EU leaders slam Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
item.description:
UN and EU leaders voiced shock on Sunday at an attack by Yemen's Houthi rebels on an airport in Saudi Arabia and warned against an escalation in the deadly conflict.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said he was "deeply shocked" by Saturday's attack on Riyadh's airport, which killed 12 people and wounded over 300, according to aviation authorities.
"Attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law. These attacks must cease immediately," Guterres said in a statement.
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen called the attack a "dangerous escalation" and said the Iran-backed group must halt strikes on civilian targets.
"These attacks by Iran's proxies are pushing the region into a spiral of violence. They are destabilizing crucial global transport and energy nodes with shockwave sent through the world," von der Leyen said.
"These murderous attacks at civilians must stop at once," she said, adding the EU stands in "solidarity with Saudi Arabia".
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said he "firmly condemns" the attack, which he described as "a terrorist act against Saudi Arabia and civil aviation".
"Our thoughts are with the victims and I send my sincere condolences to their loved ones," he wrote on X.
Meanwhile, UK Defence Minister Wes Streeting said the attacks were "contemptible" and a "dangerous escalation".

item.title: Why should the public pay the ‘penalty’ for rescuing banks?
item.description:
No government can escape responsibility for the looting of the banking sector. However, the previous Awami League government stands in a class of its own. The looting took place with every form of state patronage, while Bangladesh Bank failed spectacularly in its role as regulator. The central bank approved all kinds of wrongdoing to accommodate the demands of the government of the day.

As a result, the volume of non-performing loans (NPLs) in the country now exceeds Tk 6 trillion, accounting for 32.78 per cent of total loans. As much as 72 per cent of these bad loans are concentrated in just 10 banks.

Taken together, Bangladesh now has the highest rate of loan defaults in the world. Bangladesh Bank must bear responsibility for this.

Yet the governor of that very central bank is now saying that public money was embezzled and that the public must pay to cover the losses. In the words of Governor Mostaqur Rahman, the public will have to pay a penalty. He has even provided an estimate of the amount, and it is substantial. Speaking at an event last Saturday, he said Tk 600 billion would have to be spent every year to recover from the collapse of the banking sector. This would have to continue for the next five to eight years.

Over five years, the total cost would amount to Tk 3 trillion; over eight years, it would reach Tk 4.8 trillion. Compared with the budget for the 2026–27 fiscal year, the annual outlay would be equivalent to around 6.5 per cent of the budget.

The Bangladesh Bank governor has also offered comparisons to illustrate the scale of the expenditure. For instance, Tk 600 billion a year could be used to support 20 million families through family cards, or it could pay for the construction of two Padma Bridges.

Why should we pay the penalty?

According to the latest estimates from the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS), the penalty would amount to approximately Tk 3,432 per person, based on the country’s population.

The question is whether this money could be borrowed from a development partner instead of being taken from taxpayers. The answer is no. No development partner is likely to lend money to cover losses caused by looting in the banking sector.

We know that the World Bank has an ongoing lending programme for Bangladesh’s financial sector. The $450 million programme covers deposit protection, strengthening Bangladesh Bank’s supervisory capacity and preparations for bank restructuring. In other words, the World Bank is not providing money to cover the losses themselves. The only source left, therefore, is taxpayers’ money.

It is to be remembered that development partners never lend without conditions. The money Bangladesh is receiving from the World Bank also comes with numerous conditions. If lenders impose conditions when providing loans, why should the public have to hand over their tax money in the name of a penalty without any conditions in return?

The questions, then, are simple: why should we pay this penalty, and what will we get in return?

How much political will does the government have?

The biggest question is how much political will the government actually has to put the banking sector in order. There are certainly reasons to be sceptical.

On 9 May 2025, the interim government promulgated the Bank Resolution Ordinance. It did not allow former bank owners to regain ownership. But the law subsequently passed by the BNP government in parliament included a new provision that opened the door for former owners to take control again.

Critics argued that the provision had been inserted specifically to facilitate the return of a controversial businessman. Following strong criticism, the provision was eventually scrapped. Development partners had also raised objections.

One of the most widely discussed problems under the previous government was the entrenchment of family control over private banks. The previous administration had enabled this to facilitate looting. The public expects family dominance in the banking sector not to return.

To that end, Bangladesh Bank proposed reducing the maximum number of directors from a single family from three to two, and cutting the maximum consecutive tenure of a director from 12 years to six. It has now emerged, however, that the Financial Institutions Division (FID) of the Ministry of Finance has rejected both proposals. Instead, it has proposed reducing the maximum consecutive tenure from 12 years to nine while retaining the existing rule allowing up to three directors from the same family.

Past experience has shown that governments have retained the Financial Institutions Division ostensibly to oversee the banking sector but in practice to impose political decisions on economic policymaking. The same pattern appears to be continuing.

Yet the BNP pledged in its election manifesto to establish a commission to reform the financial sector and abolish the Financial Institutions Division under the Ministry of Finance. Implementing these two pledges after coming to power would be a major test of the government’s political will.

Here, I would like to refer to a report prepared by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 2019. The report, titled Financial Sector Stability Review, was never published because the Awami League government at the time was unhappy with its findings.

The IMF wrote: “There is a deep-rooted and persistent tendency among a section of society not to repay loans. Some influential and wealthy businesspeople have realised that the country lacks effective mechanisms to compel them to repay their loans.

Decision-making in Bangladesh’s financial sector has come under the control of influential borrowers. The situation is such that the default of just three large borrowers could cause a bank to fail.”

If that system is allowed to return, the public’s payment of the penalty will have been entirely in vain.

What mechanisms are in place to recover the money?

According to government figures, courts have ordered the seizure, attachment or freezing of assets worth approximately Tk 769.84 billion, both at home and abroad, as part of efforts to recover assets siphoned out of the country.

Of this amount, assets worth Tk 573.2593 billion are located in Bangladesh, while those held abroad are valued at Tk 196.58 billion.

We know that recovering assets held abroad is not easy. Various legal procedures must be completed. But most of the assets in question are located within the country. Recovering even these assets could provide some relief to the banking sector.

Simply announcing the formation of a task force will not reassure members of the public who are being asked to pay the penalty. They will want to see tangible progress.

Recovering losses alone will not strengthen banks

Bangladesh has so far merged five banks to form a new bank. Only time will tell whether this initiative succeeds. But mergers alone will not solve all the problems.

Malaysia, South Korea and several other countries offer examples of how to repair a weakened banking sector. The 1997 Asian financial crisis brought the banking sectors of several East Asian countries to the brink of collapse. Their recovery offers important lessons for Bangladesh.

Following the Asian financial crisis, Malaysia established Danaharta to acquire and manage non-performing loans, Danamodal to inject capital into banks, and the Corporate Debt Restructuring Committee to restructure the debts of large corporate borrowers.

At the same time, it consolidated its banking sector, reducing 51 banking institutions to 10 banking groups. In other words, it did not simply remove bad loans; it also changed banks’ capital structures and institutional framework.

During the crisis, South Korea closed several inefficient banks. The Korea Asset Management Corporation was tasked with acquiring non-performing loans. To maintain depositors’ confidence, the government temporarily guaranteed deposits held with financial institutions.

Earlier, during its banking crisis in the 1990s, Sweden established a dedicated bank support authority. It assessed the financial condition of distressed banks, injected capital into those that could be saved and took control of those that could not. Separate asset management companies, Securum and Retriva, were also established to handle impaired assets. The government published information on the condition of the banking sector and the assistance provided, making accountability an integral part of the programme.

The public has conditions too

When governments borrow from development partners, they must meet conditions attached to the loans and report on progress. The same requirements should apply when taxpayers’ money is used to rescue banks.

The government must clearly explain what reforms will be undertaken in return for this money, what results are expected, who will be held responsible if the reforms fail, and what punishment has been imposed on those responsible for the previous crisis.

The banking sector needs money to recover. But the public must also be shown how much the sector will change in return for that money.

item.title: 10 Dhaka–Riyadh flights cancelled after attack on Saudi airport
item.description:
Ten flights from Dhaka to Riyadh have been cancelled following a Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi capital. A total of 3,431 passengers were scheduled to travel on these flights.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) provided the information on Monday morning.

According to CAAB, the cancelled flights include two operated by Biman Bangladesh Airlines, two by US-Bangla Airlines, three by Saudia and three by Riyadh Air.

Identities of 26 Bangladeshis killed or injured in airport attack in Saudi Arabia confirmed

In a press release yesterday, Sunday, the state-owned airline said passengers would be informed of the revised schedules for its two cancelled flights at 12:00 pm Monday. Biman suspended flights BG 339 and BG 340 on Saturday night.

Following the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday night, the airport suspended operations. This disrupted air connectivity between Dhaka and Riyadh. By Sunday, CAAB had reported the cancellation of eight flights from Dhaka, leaving 2,951 passengers stranded.

Updating its information on Monday morning, CAAB said the number of cancelled flights had risen to 10. The number of affected passengers had also increased.

Bangladesh condemns attack on Saudi airport, seeks details of victims

The attack on Riyadh airport has created uncertainty over flight operations. Passengers have been advised to contact their airlines to check the latest status of their flights.

According to flight-tracking website Flightradar24, all flights bound for Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled.

A Reuters report said the decision followed attacks and explosions at the Saudi capital’s international airport.

Reuters reported the suspension of flights at Riyadh International Airport, adding that airport authorities had advised passengers to contact their respective airlines before travelling to the airport and to check the latest status of their flights.
